beats.narration_text: This week the V L A security project moves from planning into execution. The plan targets Open V L A seven B on the LIBERO benchmark, but the two fine-tuned checkpoints need thirty gigabytes of disk and over sixteen gigabytes of V R A M. Can two engineers on Windows laptops run twenty hertz closed-loop robot experiments anyway?

props.command: How do we run 20 Hz closed-loop OpenVLA-7B experiments on LIBERO from Windows laptops that cannot hold a 15 GB checkpoint or a 24 GB GPU?
output: Kaggle T4 x2 cloud inference via auto-discovered tunnel

beats.narration_text: Here is the week's core decision. Running Open V L A seven B locally is beyond laptop hardware, so we split the system in two: the physics simulation stays local for low latency, and the model moves to a free Kaggle cloud server. Both engineers now drive fifteen-gigabyte checkpoints from their laptops.

beats.narration_text: The architecture is a clean split. A local rollout engine steps the MuJoCo physics simulator and renders two hundred twenty-four pixel R G B observations. The client serializes each frame as a lossless base64 P N G, sends it through an auto-discovered Cloudflare tunnel, and a Kaggle T four server runs F P sixteen inference. The seven degree of freedom action comes back and the episode is saved for attacks and defenses.

phases.label: Local MuJoCo rollout
phases.desc: LIBERO task stepping in the 20 Hz loop

beats.narration_text: One measurement shows why the server needed tuning. Kaggle mounts datasets over F U S E, and cold-loading model shards page-faults at sixty-five megabytes per second. Our warm safetensors routine streams all four shards into the Linux page cache first, cutting checkpoint load time from three minutes thirty-six seconds down to forty-one seconds.

Two more findings shaped the final server. Loading both checkpoints at once exhausted the T four's memory and thrashed system R A M, so exactly one model runs per session, sharded across both G P Us with fifteen gigabytes of headroom. And the tunnel's live U R L is pushed to an ntfy topic, so local clients auto-discover the server with zero copy-paste. On Windows, four known incompatibilities are fixed automatically by the setup script.

terms.definition: Dual-load OOMs both T4s; a single model sharded across GPUs leaves ~15 GB headroom.
Cloudflare URL pushed to ntfy.sh; local clients auto-discover, no copy-paste.
git longpaths, editable __init__.py, weights_only=False, mujoco.dll copy - all automated.

beats.narration_text: The result is a clean separation of concerns for the rest of the project. Simulation and data collection stay local, inference stays remote on F P sixteen T four compute, and the attack and defense code stays model-agnostic, talking only to the client and the rollout engine. Next: record clean baseline rollouts, collect fifteen trajectories per task, and implement the token and attention hooks.
